title: Outcome effects and Erie’s twin aims
shortTitle: Outcome effects and Erie’s twin aims
summary: The outcome inquiry asks how a difference between state and federal treatment affects the enforcement of state-created rights. Hanna relates the inquiry to discouraging forum shopping and unequal administration of law.
notes: Almost any procedural choice can affect who wins after a dispute arises. That observation alone does not decide whether the federal court must adopt the state practice.

sections.Meaning: The outcome inquiry asks how a difference between state and federal treatment affects the enforcement of state-created rights. Hanna relates the inquiry to discouraging forum shopping and unequal administration of law.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the practical effect of applying the alternative rules, especially at the point parties choose a forum. York’s limitations problem is an important example. Then consider the later qualifications in Byrd and Hanna.
